findings.title: NPE fix is incomplete: getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference a possibly-null delegate
findings.body: The PR fixes the concurrent-deletion NPE only in getSubGroupsCount() by null-checking the result of modelSupplier.get(). However, the three getSubGroupsStream(...) overloads in GroupAdapter (lines 256, 262 and 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. modelSupplier.get() resolves to cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId()), which returns null when the group has just been deleted by another thread/session — exactly the race this PR is meant to fix. Any code path that hits those overloads on a cached group that was concurrently deleted (e.g. paginated or searched subgroup listings) will still throw a NullPointerException. The same guard (null-check or a consistent 'not found' handling) should be applied to these methods.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now silently returns null for a deleted group, diverging from the adapter's other not-found handling
findings.body: When the underlying group no longer exists, getSubGroupsCount() now returns null, whereas every other delegate-resolving path in GroupAdapter (getDelegateForUpdate() at line 61 and isUpdated() at line 74) throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database"). The null value propagates to callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount(), which sets it on GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(...), so admin REST responses can now contain a null subGroupCount where a number was previously always present (or a clear error was raised). Any consumer that unboxes the Long (e.g. `rep.getSubGroupCount() > 0` style checks in the admin UI or other code) will throw a NullPointerException. A consistent behavior — throwing the same IllegalStateException, or returning 0L for a vanished group — would be safer than leaking null through the API.

findings.title: Concurrent-read test never joins the reader thread, so the assertion races and can miss the very exception it checks for
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti(), the background reader thread is started at line 139 and only stopped cooperatively via `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155, but it is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` at line 157. Consequences: (1) an exception thrown by a read request that is still in flight when the assertion runs is silently dropped, so the test can pass even if the NPE it is meant to catch still occurs — making it flaky-pass and useless as a regression test; (2) the non-daemon reader thread can keep issuing requests after the test method returns, leaking into subsequently executing tests and potentially causing unrelated failures. The thread reference should be kept and joined (or the loop bounded with a latch/await) before asserting on caughtExceptions. Additionally, since the thread may not even start before all deletions finish, the race may not be exercised at all on fast machines.
